title: Count Active Cache Entries per Query
statement:
A cache holds `n` data items. Item `i` is inserted into the cache at time `t[i]` and stays there for `d[i]` units of time, so it is present during the half-open interval `[t[i], t[i] + d[i])`: it is in the cache at time `t[i]`, and gone again at time `t[i] + d[i]`.

You are given `q` query times. For each query time `x`, report how many items are in the cache at time `x`.

Queries are independent, and times are integers.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `q`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains two integers `t[i]` and `d[i]`.
Each of the next `q` lines contains one integer, a query time `x`.
outputFormat: Print `q` lines. Line `i` is the number of items in the cache at the `i`-th query time.

examples.explanation: The items occupy [1,4), [2,7) and [6,8). At 0 nothing is in the cache. At 1 only the first. At 3 the first two. At 4 the first has expired, leaving one. At 6 the second and third. At 7 only the third. At 8 nothing.
Both items occupy [5,6). At time 5 both are present, at 6 both are gone, and at 4 neither has arrived yet.

hints: Checking every item for every query is `O(n * q)`, which is too slow at `10^5` each. What do you need to know about the items, as a function of `x` alone?
An item is active at `x` exactly when it has already been inserted (`t ≤ x`) and has not yet expired (`t + d > x`). So the answer is (items with `t ≤ x`) minus (items with `t + d ≤ x`).
Sort the insertion times and the expiry times separately, then answer each query with two binary searches.
